alice: Heads-up — I noticed a perf regression after enabling the new FP8 calibration profile on the dedicated cluster. Quick profiling below, reproduced on a scale test node.

alice: ```
# before (int8 baseline, commit abc110)
model: llama-3-8b, seq_len=512, batch=8, hw=H100
tokens/sec: 28.4k

# after (fp8 calib enabled, commit abc123)
tokens/sec: 19.1k  <-- ~33% drop
GPU mem: +1.1GB
kv copy time spikes in profile: kv_copy_ms=12.4 -> 38.2
stack: runtime/kernel_selector: chose CUTLASS_FP8 path
```

ben: Which commit exactly and did you run the arch probe script? can you paste the runtime logs around kernel selection?

alice: commit abc123 (merge of fp8-calib). Ran `./tools/probe_arch.sh` on the node, it printed sm=80, but runtime log shows it selected cutlass FP8 kernels assuming sm=86. Full snippet:

alice: ```
[2026-02-14T10:22:11Z] arch_detector: cuda_driver=535.54, reported_sm=90
[2026-02-14T10:22:11Z] arch_probe: normalized_sm=80 -> family=sm80
[2026-02-14T10:22:11Z] kernel_selector: using policy=perf, chosen_family=CUTLASS_FP8
[2026-02-14T10:22:11Z] kv_cache: layout=packed, memcopy_strategy=async
```

carol: That mismatch looks like the probe rounding bug we saw last quarter. If runtime normalizes reported_sm -> 80 incorrectly, it can enable a CUTLASS micro-kernel optimized for short matrices. Those kernels are great for short context but they do extra KV packing which kills long-seq throughput.

carol: TL;DR: CUTLASS_FP8 path does extra per-token packing for cache alignment. That + our batching heuristic (auto) is shrinking batches into many small launches which massively increases per-token overhead for seq=2048 workloads.

dinesh: Quick experiment: force kernel family to Triton and run the same load. I toggled env var REDWOOD_KERNEL_FAMILY=triton on a repro node. Results:

dinesh: ```
# forced triton
tokens/sec: 25.9k
GPU mem: baseline
kv_copy_ms: 9.8

# forced cutlass
tokens/sec: 18.6k
kv_copy_ms: 40.1
```

dinesh: So Triton restores most throughput but CUTLASS_FP8 reduces mem copies at smaller seqs but regresses large seqs.

ben: Do we have a fast fix? Maybe change the batching heuristic to prefer larger continuous batches for FP8 kernels or skip the CUTLASS_FP8 family for seq>1024?

carol: Two orthogonal fixes:
- short-term: disable CUTLASS_FP8 for rollout (env override or runtime flag) and roll back calibration gating for long-seq customers.
- mid-term: adjust kernel selector to include a sequence-length-aware score (penalize packing overhead when seq>1024) and fix probe rounding bug so arch detection maps to correct kernel families.

alice: I also saw KV cache thrash when autoscaling burst kicks in — workers flush/repack on fallback path. Need to make fallback path preserve KV layout to avoid full repack.

dinesh: Build flags to try next: `-DENABLE_FP8_PACKING=OFF -DUSE_CUTLASS_KERNELS=ON` vs `-DUSE_TRITON_KERNELS=ON -DENABLE_FP8_CUTLASS=OFF`. I ran a quick local build with `-DENABLE_FP8_PACKING=OFF` and got tokens/sec 23.5k (better).

ci-bot: perf job /ci/jobs/1729 produced delta: -31% tokens/sec on 8-node perf-sim for config fp8_calib=true, threshold -15%. See: http://ci.internal/1729 (artifacts attached).

ben: Sounds like action items. Who wants to own short-term rollback toggle?

alice: I can push an emergency config flag to disable the FP8 packing path and gate the rollout for the Dedicated cohort. Will do a PR.

carol: I'll open a kernel-selector PR to add seq_len into the scoring function and fix the arch rounding. I'll include unit tests that simulate sm mapping edge cases.

dinesh: I'll prototype a non-repacking fallback that preserves KV layout and experiment with a batching tweak: prefer max_batch_time window of 5ms for FP8 to avoid tiny launches.

ben: Assigning: alice -> rollback toggle PR, carol -> selector + probe fix, dinesh -> kv fallback + batching tweak. Add perf tests to the CI job to catch regression.

alice: PR link (WIP): https://git.redwood/re/runtime/pulls/482 — includes env var `REDWOOD_DISABLE_FP8_PACKING=1` and an emergency switch in config.

carol: I'll add a new CI perf threshold that includes seq=2048, batch=4 for fp8 paths to prevent silent regressions.

dinesh: One more note: when toggling between Triton and CUTLASS I saw memory allocator fragmentation. Recommend adding allocator reset on kernel-family switch during warmup.

alice: Ok all — I'll merge the toggle behind a feature flag and run a canary tomorrow morning. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
